transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Louise Schiavone.
Due to a stalemate over fossil fuels, U.N. climate talks in Entalia, Turkey, concluded
today without an overarching agreement.
At issue, the role of fossil fuels in raising the temperature of the planet, Russia and
Saudi Arabia led the resistance, Australian Chris Bowen led the COP31 negotiations.
Nearly 200 nations were involved in the talks in Turkey, the United States was not.
More than a thousand Delta Airlines flights faced delays today, the airline reported problems
with an automated system used to calculate the weight and balance of its planes.
NPR's Andrea Schute reports.
In a statement, Delta Airlines said its teams are using manual workarounds to safely get
flights off the ground while they continue to restore automation.
Earlier this morning, the outage prompted the Federal Aviation Administration to call
a temporary ground delay for Delta flights in Atlanta, its hub to manage congestion that
has since been lifted.
The problems come just over a week after the FAA called a nationwide ground stop that halted
takeoffs for more than four hours.
Officials said some maintenance work on an aging system was to blame.
With Thanksgiving approaching, AAA projects some six million people will be flying this
week.
Andrea Schute, NPR News.
A survey of business executives suggest inflation in the U.S. economy may get worse before it
gets better.
NPR's Scott Horsley reports on findings from the Cleveland Federal Reserve Bank.
CEOs surveyed by the bank say on average they expect to raise their prices by 3.7 percent
over the next year.
That's a bigger price hike than executives were projecting six months ago, but it's still
not big enough to cover the higher costs they expect their own companies to face.
Researchers project their costs will climb by more than 4 percent.
That's also up from the previous survey.
The Federal Reserve tries to limit inflation to just 2 percent per year, but prices have
been climbing faster than that for over five years now.
The central bank is expected to raise its benchmark interest rate next month in an effort
to tamp down demand and bring price hikes under control.
Scott Horsley, NPR News, Washington.
Michigan's Senator-elect Abdullah Al-Sayed says passing Medicare for all with the support
of President Trump would be the ultimate Trump card.
On social media, the Democrat posted a mock-up of a gold-colored Trump care card and stating
guaranteed health care for every American from cradle to grave.
President Trump took a screenshot and then shared it on his own social media platform.
Al-Sayed told NBC's Meet the Press today that he's encouraged the president is interested
and he personally doesn't really care what it's called.
This is NPR News in Washington.
Federal documents show tech giant META has considered working with schools across the
country to get more teens on the social media site Instagram.
NPR's Katie McHugh reports that experts are warning the plan could make teens less safe
online.
META called the plan Project Gryffindor.
It encourages students to add school banners to their profiles and use directories to connect
with other classmates.
META launched the school partnership program in 2025.
Nearly 17,000 schools have signed up.
Publicly, META said the program is designed to improve student safety, help schools report
bullying and keep families informed about school activities.
Yet, cybersecurity experts say the program increases teens' vulnerability to scammers
and hackers, who often try to access their connections for blackmail and sex torsion
schemes.
And experts say the program's student directories will make this easier to do.
META disputes his criticisms, saying the program provides meaningful safety protections.
Katie McHugh, NPR News, New York.
A Vincent van Gogh landscape painted weeks before his death has sold for $190.4 million
at auction.
The painting Chateauneur en Fleur exceeded its $180 million estimated at Sotheby's auction
in New York in recent days.
Van Gogh painted Chateauneur en Fleur after his release from a psychiatric asylum in May
of 1890, and he took his own life two months later.
Fourteen-year Denver Broncos pro and Super Bowl star turned ESPN broadcast veteran Tom
Jackson has died.
The network announced his death today.
He was 75.
I'm Louise Skivone, NPR News, Washington.

topics.text: U.N. climate talks in Turkey end without agreement over fossil fuels, with Russia and Saudi Arabia resisting
Delta Airlines suffers automated system outage delaying over a thousand flights; Atlanta ground delay lifted
Business executives expect higher prices and costs, pointing to inflation worsening, per Cleveland Fed survey
Senator-elect Abdullah Al-Sayed says Medicare for all backed by Trump would be the ultimate Trump card
Federal documents reveal Meta's Project Gryffindor plan to get teens on Instagram through schools
Van Gogh landscape Chateau Noir en Fleur sells for $190.4 million at Sotheby's auction in New York
ESPN broadcaster and former Denver Broncos star Tom Jackson dies at age 75
